labctl.notes: RETRONET BRIDGE (2026-08-22): n0 is a tap on vmbr-rn (NOT slirp); the guest is a DHCP client on the reserved 10.99.0.16/24 with NO default route (rn-tapnet.sh + the fail-closed guard chain BEOSRN-IN, which aborts the launch if it does not verify). PS/2 RELATIVE pointer (pointerRel) -- R5 has no absolute tablet, and it applies its own acceleration, so scripted pointer work must be closed-loop (slam to 0,0, step, screendump, correct). exec = telnet_unix_e: labctl exec beos over BeOS R5's OWN telnetd at 10.99.0.16:23 over the bridge (no hostfwd, no agent in the guest, no port forward), user baron, password from the station dir's telnet-exec.passwd which the launcher writes from registry/local.env; client /root/sunexec.py with SUN_RC=$? because R5's login shell is bash. R5's ftpd is on :21 the same way for file transfer. KDL/kernel debug still lands on serial.log. See docs/lab/retronet/STATION-beos.md.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# beos (VMID 143) - BeOS R5 Professional 5.0.3, the original behind haiku.
#   TCG (R5 #GPs under KVM: unhandled MSRs), pentium3, 1 CPU, 512 MB, IDE
#   qcow2 on an MBR partition, std VGA at the vesa-settings 1024x768x16.
#   ABSOLUTE pointer since 2026-08-31: -device kh-ramabs writes app_server's own
#   pointer coordinate in guest RAM (point32le) and publishes it with one 1-unit
#   PS/2 nudge -- no adapter change, no device-set change. Runs its OWN build at
#   /opt/qemu-beos rather than the host package, because the golden had to be
#   cold re-baked anyway (the old one carried pve's pbs-state section).
#   RETRONET: rtl8139 on a tap
#   on vmbr-rn (DHCP-reserved 10.99.0.16, no default route, guard chain
#   BEOSRN-IN); ne2k_pci was the NIC until 2026-08-23 and had to go -- R5's
#   etherpci driver storms 'bad next packet' and dies under a real page load.
#   VERBATIM launcher with conditional -loadvm golden. Two fixes live INSIDE the
#   volume: config_manager/isa removed (PnP BIOS call page-faults input_server
#   under SeaBIOS) and multiprocessor_support disabled (PCI IRQs via the PIC).

museum.blurb: Be Inc.'s BeOS R5 (2000) — the multithreaded media OS behind Haiku's yellow tabs, running as it shipped.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. BeOS R5 Professional 5.0.3 installed from the archive.org Pro CD onto an MBR BFS partition; TCG-only (KVM #GP). Archetype: beige-tower-crt; a BeBox would be the ideal model but R5 x86 shipped on commodity PCs. On the retronet since 2026-08-23: rtl8139 on vmbr-rn, DHCP 10.99.0.16, browsing the museum corpus in NetPositive, and signed in to the museum's own ICQ gateway as UIN 50000 with ICBM .71 (the BeCQ successor, 2001) over the pre-OSCAR UDP-4000 door — the only station on the fleet that uses it; HiveBot greets a visitor about half a minute after the client signs on. See docs/lab/retronet/STATION-beos.md.

stationEnv.SH_FIXTURE_DESC: BeOS R5 1024x768x16 desktop: Deskbar top-right; Terminal and NetPositive on the museum corpus page http://spacejam.com/ (both opened by UserBootscript); ICBM .71 signed on as UIN 50000, roster window showing Online/Available and NO message window; pointer parked at 69,747 on bare desktop, clear of the page (sprite origin 68,747 plus the (1,0) hotspot). That pointer value is OPERATIONALLY LOAD-BEARING, not decoration: kh-ramabs' connect probe re-states where the guest already is, so 69,747 is what the device reports VERIFIED at on every future connection, and a reader who expects some other number will misread a healthy probe as a fault. The absent message window is deliberate: HiveBot greets every sign-on about 30s later, so a cold boot produces one or not purely as a function of elapsed time, and this is the scene the incumbent golden shipped.

launcherParity.reason: tracked verbatim launcher is the deployed launcher. Absolute pointer CUT OVER 2026-08-31: a `-chardev socket` plus `-device kh-ramabs` writing app_server's own pointer coordinate. kh-ramabs registers NO VMStateDescription and touches no emulated hardware, so it adds no section to the migration stream and does not change the device set. What DID force a golden re-bake is the BINARY: the 2026-08-23 golden was baked under the host pve-qemu-kvm package and carries a Proxmox-only `pbs-state` vmstate section, which a standalone build refuses with `Unknown section or instance 'pbs-state' 0`. beos was the wave's only station on the host package, so it cost one cold re-bake -- done 2026-08-31 12:12:00 under /opt/qemu-beos, and RESTORE-PROVEN there: three loadvm cycles through the guard's own checkpoint-guard-proof.sh (byte-identical, byte-identical, byte-identical), the third on a FRESH QEMU PROCESS because a warm restore can pass where the visitor path fails. Each cycle also asserts the CURSOR ORIGIN returns to 68,747, which the guard's whole-frame SSIM cannot see (a cursor move scores 0.999756, i.e. 'unchanged') and which matters here because kh-ramabs' connect probe re-states wherever the golden left the pointer. BINARY AND GOLDEN ARE NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVERTIBLE -- the new golden cannot be restored by the host binary and the old one cannot be restored by the fork build -- so BEOS_QEMU and the golden file roll back together. The rollback has been EXERCISED, not merely argued: the pre-cutover backup was restored under /usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 on 2026-08-31 and came back to the fixture scene. INSTALL ORDER IS BINDING: QEMU binary before the launcher (`-device kh-ramabs` is an unknown device on an older binary and QEMU refuses to start), and the streamhost binary before the env fixture (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=ramabs panics an older daemon at startup).

pointerRamAddress.derivedAgainstGolden: 2026-08-31 12:12:00 cold re-bake under /opt/qemu-beos (VM_CLOCK 0000:26:11.140, tag `golden` in beos-golden.qcow2)
pointerRamAddress.note: Guest-physical address of BeOS R5 app_server's own pointer coordinate -- the input the kh-ramabs control object writes, as two little-endian int32. Valid ONLY for the golden named in derivedAgainstGolden: `loadvm golden` restores RAM verbatim, so the address is fixed for the life of THAT checkpoint and no longer, and a re-bake moves it. Re-derive after every re-bake with the four-sample pmemsave bias search in docs/lab/BEOS-ABSOLUTE-POINTER.md. THE SEARCH ALONE CANNOT PICK IT: this bake returned 16 tracking addresses in four bias families, and the (1,0) family alone held four -- 0x02a8ff44, 0x02a904e8, 0x03a5fae4 and 0x03a5faec -- every one of which tracks the pointer perfectly. Only a WRITE TEST separates them, and kh-ramabs' own connect-time probe is that test: it writes a deliberately wrong value, reads it back to prove the write landed, then requires the guest to correct it via the injected nudge. Exactly one address passed (probefail=0, pos=69,747); the other three failed identically with 'probe wanted 69,747, guest holds 77,740'. A stale address degrades this station to its relative path rather than corrupting guest memory.

qemuBuild.base: QEMU 11.0.2 (the same version as the host pve-qemu-kvm 11.0.2-1, so machine type pc-i440fx-11.0 is unchanged)
qemuBuild.note: Built from fork c5449c80 with NOTHING applied on top: that tip already carries the fast-poll patch (0001) and the shared kh-ramabs device (0007, including this station's point32le layout) as commits, so applying patch files as well would have been a chance to misapply them. Recorded as a FORK COMMIT rather than a patch list on purpose -- the tip also carries 0002-0005 and 0008, all inert for beos but present in the binary, so a patches[] field would describe intent rather than the artifact. Same provenance shape as rhapsody, macos753 and hpuxvue. Fast-poll is NOT optional on a standalone build: on the host package it arrives as pve quilt slot 0047, and a build without it silently drops this tile to the stock 30 ms display scan. binarySha256 is read from the INSTALLED file at the prefix, not from a build log.
